quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 40 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: Small vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast and how far away a small vehicle is, like a motorcycle. Do not assume that drivers of larger vehicles can accurately see your speed and location.

questions.question: Part of your normal scanning routine while riding should include:

options.text: Constantly looking in the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Frequent rearview mirror checks.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal scanning routine. Also check your mirrors before changing lanes, when stopping at an intersection, and before slowing down.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane is ending.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists pass another vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, motorcyclists in a group should pass another vehicle one at a time. Each rider must finish passing before the next one begins.

questions.question: You have a better chance of avoiding serious injury in a crash if you wear:
questions.correctAnswerText: Face or eye protection.
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best protection against injury while riding. A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield can help protect your face from injury in a crash.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are separated by:
questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid line means you cannot pass. A dashed line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A red octagonal sign is always a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Doesn't mean that they will properly yield to you.
Guarantees that they will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doesn't mean that they will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that eye contact with another driver means they will yield to you. A driver may look directly at you and still not see you.

questions.question: When wearing a jacket for protection, the jacket should:

options.text: Be loose-fitting and flap in the wind while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly.
questions.explanation: Riding clothes should protect you and keep you comfortable. Jackets and pants should fit snugly so they don't flap in the wind, but not so tight that they limit your movement.

questions.question: Riding on ______ may provide poor traction.
questions.correctAnswerText: Pavement markings
questions.explanation: Traction can be poor on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement; gravel roads; lane markings; and steel plates or manhole covers.

questions.question: Unlike other substances, alcohol:

options.text: Must be digested before entering the bloodstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: Enters the bloodstream very quickly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested first. It passes directly through the stomach and small intestine walls into the bloodstream. It reaches the brain quickly and affects your ability to ride.

questions.question: To properly control a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Use your arms to hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit with your arms slightly bent and use them to steer, not to hold yourself up. Keep your knees against the gas tank. This helps you balance during turns and control the motorcycle.

questions.question: You should use a larger cushion of space:

options.text: When it is colder than usual.
When you are following other motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: When roads are slippery.
questions.explanation: Use a two-second following distance in normal conditions. Use more space when conditions make it harder to stop, such as wet or icy roads.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Only stop if there is other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop. Yield to all traffic and pedestrians. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When turning, you should:

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head to look through the turn.
Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to see where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon. Turning your shoulders can cause you to steer off course.

questions.question: Improper braking:

options.text: Is not a concern because motorcycles have two brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Causes many motorcycle crashes.
questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Using the correct braking technique is important for safe riding.

questions.question: You have been drinking alcohol. If you wait one hour for each drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
Alcohol effects may still remain in your body.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still remain in your body.
questions.explanation: The body removes about one drink per hour. But alcohol can still build up in your body. Your skills and judgment can still be impaired even if you wait.

questions.question: If a motorcycle rider takes a turn too fast, they may:

options.text: Have better control of the motorcycle.
Lose control and leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lose control and leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast causes you to lose control. The motorcycle may cross into another lane or go off the road.

questions.question: In areas with potential dangers, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Cover the clutch and both brake levers to react faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and both brake levers to react faster.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, schools, and construction zones, slow down. Cover the clutch and both brake levers. This reduces your reaction time in an emergency.

questions.question: Your motorcycle is weaving on bridge gratings. You should:

options.text: Speed up to cross the surface faster.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves on bridge gratings, stay calm. Keep a steady speed and go straight across. Do not weave side to side, as this is dangerous.

questions.question: A person is considered intoxicated at a blood alcohol content (BAC) of ____.
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Virginia, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means a person is intoxicated. It is illegal to drive a motor vehicle while intoxicated.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same location as on your motorcycle.
Take it out on the highway right away.
Get familiar with it in a controlled area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get familiar with it in a controlled area first.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, learn where all the controls are. Practice riding it in a safe, controlled area before going on the road.

questions.question: If vehicles are on both sides of your motorcycle, which lane position is usually safest?
questions.correctAnswerText: Center
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best. A good rider adjusts their position based on road and traffic conditions. If vehicles are on both sides, the center position is usually safest.

questions.question: Which material provides the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather and sturdy synthetic materials offer the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: As your motorcycle speeds up, you will:

options.text: Need to shift up through the gears.
Need to shift down through the gears.
Need to put the motorcycle into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need to shift up through the gears.
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle goes faster, you must shift into higher gears.

questions.question: It is illegal to operate a motorcycle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: In California, drivers age 21 and older cannot operate a motorcycle with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Drivers under 21 cannot operate with a BAC of 0.01 percent or higher. Riding may be unsafe even below the legal limit.

questions.question: Which fabric provides the most protection for motorcyclists?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants provide the best protection when riding.

questions.question: When making a normal stop on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, use the front and rear brakes at the same time and downshift.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, the effects:

options.text: Are less dangerous than using either alone.
Can be stronger than using either alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be stronger than using either alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, can impair your riding. Combining drugs with alcohol can make the effects more dangerous.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing down or stopping. Using both brakes helps you stop quickly.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of a pre-ride inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Inspecting the paint.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, chassis, and stands.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous for a motorcycle rider to ride directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: The other vehicle may block your way to escape.
Other drivers can easily see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other vehicle may block your way to escape.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. The other vehicle could hit you or block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a straight road, what happens?

options.text: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You must release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually keep control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can usually control your motorcycle if it stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: A motorcycle's horn is ________ a car's horn.
questions.correctAnswerText: Quieter than
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's horn is not as loud as a car's horn. Use your horn when needed, but do not rely on it to stay safe.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both the front and rear brakes with controlled pressure at the same time.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, should you move away from it in your lane?

options.text: Yes, because you will be farther away.
No, because it may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
No, because it has no effect on safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because it may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move away from a passing vehicle. Doing so may encourage the other driver to move back into your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your entire face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield cannot replace a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: A "wobble" (shaking of the front wheel and handlebars) is usually caused by:

options.text: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight distribution.
The front wheel not being attached properly to the frame.
Hitting something with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight distribution.
questions.explanation: A wobble is when the front wheel and handlebars shake side to side. It is usually caused by improper weight distribution, wrong tire pressure, or unsuitable accessories.

questions.question: If you and another vehicle reach an intersection at the same time and there are no signs or traffic lights, who must yield?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go.
You should go through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When braking on a motorcycle, which brake should you apply?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. Using only the rear brake may prevent you from learning how to use the front brake properly when you need to stop quickly.
